relations.note: 079 states the Kakeya maximal conjecture in every dimension and full Hausdorff dimension for every Euclidean Kakeya set; 074 claims the maximal conjecture in three dimensions and the dimension conjecture in four.
079 states the Bochner–Riesz conjecture in every dimension; 078 claims it in three dimensions.
079 gives Fourier extension from the sphere and the compact paraboloid; 077 claims it for every compact smooth positively curved surface in ℝ³, so 079 covers 077’s sphere and paraboloid cases.
Both are about the three-dimensional incompressible Navier–Stokes equations with a smooth external force: S01 claims finite-time blowup, 376 universal computation.

Both 018 papers say they use the classification of finite simple groups: number fields, “The argument uses the classification of finite simple groups” (build/sections/finite-groups.tex, line 4); function fields, “The proof uses the classification of finite simple groups” (build/paper/A-finite-groups.tex, line 12).
relations.label: uses CFSG, which AX01 formalizes in Lean (our reading)

relations.note: AX02 cites both of OpenAI’s zero-free preprints: “OpenAI has released two proofs of nonvanishing in a fixed half-plane: Re s > 7/8 … and Re s > 11/12” (DedekindZeta.tex, line 104, Hexagon 2610.00200 v2 source). For the rational numbers its 31/32 is weaker than 003’s 7/8, so it is not an independent check of 003.
